alignments.note: Waw takes and (rule 14).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary, headed on the lexical predicate offer (rules 17, 24).
Object suffix takes the pronoun it (rule 18).
לִפְנֵי fused into the single before; rule 30's one-English-word condition is met, and the unit heads on פָּנֶה, the morpheme carrying the lexeme.
Divine name.
Waw takes and (rule 14).
Verb rendered as light verb plus complement; make alone makes anything, so the head is atonement (rule 44).
עַל is rendered for here; align the word the ASV wrote (rule 11).
Suffix takes the object pronoun her (rule 18).
Waw takes and (rule 14).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliaries, headed on the lexical predicate cleansed (rules 17, 24).
Preposition takes from (rule 11).
Construct noun with a supplied the, no article morpheme standing in the chain (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes of + blood, discontinuous around the suffix's pronoun (rules 19, 25).
Suffix takes the possessive her (rule 18).
Explicit subject demonstrative takes only its own English; the construction-supplied copula goes to the predicate (rule 20).
Predicate of the verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula together with its noun and the supplied the (rules 20, 29).
Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun and relative and heads on the pronoun (rule 41).

The participle is the nomen rectum of תּוֹרַת, so the relational for the ASV writes for that construct relation is its own (rule 19); the unit is discontinuous around the article's her that (rule 25) and heads on the lexeme-bearing beareth (rule 24).

The ASV writes no word for this preposition's own relation: whether is the opening member of the correlative pair the disjunction אוֹ is rendered by, not a rendering of לְ. Rule 14's exception hands an opening correlative to another morpheme only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says — a present negative for neither, the מִן of a range for both — and a preposition meaning for is not what whether says; standing in the slot where a for would have stood is position, not sense. So the preposition is unrepresented (rule 40), exactly as the second לְ of the pair is. The competing reading, taken by the earlier alignment, gives whether to this לְ on positional grounds; a third reading leaves whether added under rule 30 (rule 8).
The ASV writes a male indefinitely, so the article assimilated into the pointed preposition has no the of its own (rules 12, 29).
Noun with the indefinite article that belongs to the nominal it determines (rule 15).

The ASV renders this one disjunction by the correlative pair whether ... or, so both English words belong to אוֹ's single discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective (rules 14, 25). No other morpheme has a claim on whether: the לְ's of the two members are prepositions the ASV spends no word on. The competing reading gives whether to the first לְ, or leaves it added (rule 8).
The ASV writes no second for; the preposition of the second member has no English (rule 40).
The ASV writes a female indefinitely, so this assimilated article has no the (rules 12, 29).
Noun with its indefinite article (rule 15).

review_notes: Correction: whether (t032) is moved from the first לְ (s021) to אוֹ (s024), which now holds the discontinuous correlative pair whether ... or headed on or, and s021 joins s025 as unrepresented. Rule 14 lets a morpheme other than the connective take an opening correlative only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says; a preposition meaning for is not what whether says, so the pair stays with the disjunction that is written. Every other unit is retained as accepted.

The law for her that beareth is divided under rules 19 and 41: the substantival article carries her that and heads on the pronoun, while the participle, as the nomen rectum of תּוֹרַת, carries the relational for together with beareth and heads on the lexeme.
Both assimilated [הַ] tokens are unrepresented because the ASV writes a male and a female indefinitely (rules 12, 29).
